newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish shares firm in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish shares firm in quiet trade.

text.p: Irish share prices firmed in light afternoon trade on Friday though traders said activity was dampened by the absence of U.S. players because of the Independence Day holiday.
"It is fairly quiet with the U.S. market closed," one dealer said. "There were some buyers around this morning but it's been fairly dull this afternoon."
By 1600 GMT, the ISEQ index of Irish shares was up 26.03 points or 0.76 percent at 3,451.16.
Dealers said the main banking stocks saw some interest and Bank of Ireland gained four pence to 757 while Allied Irish Banks edged up 4.5 pence to 543.
Among industrial stocks, Smurfit gained two pence to 193, Independent Newspapers added five pence to 400 and DCC gained five pence to 405.
Traders reported some interest in Waterford Foods which dealt up three pence to 145 ahead of next Friday's special shareholder meeting to vote on its proposed merger with Avonmore.
A 75 percent majority of those attending and voting at the meeting is required to approve the merger.
Mackie, whose shares resumed trading today after a recent suspension, lost 1.03571 to 0.61429 after announcing a downward revision to its results last month.
Kingspan, which yesterday announced it was buying the Rom group of companies for just over two million punts, gained 10 pence to 825.
